rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. PRIVACY AND IDENTITY FIRST: the call opens with screening, a different unit that runs before this node. Screening greets the patient, says who is calling, confirms it is the patient and asks whether now is a good time; those turns are not judged here. Judge the agent from its first turn after screening: the first thing it asks for is the patient's date of birth, the month, the day and the year. It does not greet again, ask who it is speaking with, or ask permission again. It never states, reads back, spells or hints at the date of birth on file before the patient has said it themselves, and it does not ask the patient to confirm the date they gave ("is that correct?" after the date of birth is NOT MET; a bare "Thank you." or stating once the date the patient just gave is correct). No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility before the patient has given their date of birth.
2. HONOURS THE RETRACTION IF NOT YET BOOKED: in the NOT-YET-BOOKED branch, after the retraction the agent does not proceed as if the choice still stood: it does not ask the patient to confirm the booking, does not say it will go ahead and book, and does not announce the appointment as set as though the retraction had not been heard. One exception, because the save can complete in the moment between the choice and the retraction: in its FIRST turn after the retraction the agent may acknowledge the request not to book and say, once, that the appointment had already been set before the request arrived, then give the number to change it ("I understand, but that one had already gone through; to change it, call the clinic on the number"). A success statement that ignores the retraction ("Great, you're all set" with no acknowledgement of the request), or one in any later turn, is NOT MET. Otherwise the call ends without a booking; the platform's "I'm sorry we bothered you" line is a normal ending. In the ALREADY-BOOKED branch this criterion is MET so long as no second, new booking is stated after the retraction. If the caller never retracts after choosing an option in the transcript, this criterion is NOT MET.
3. NO CONTRADICTION IF ALREADY BOOKED: in the ALREADY-BOOKED branch, and after the exception in criterion 2, the agent never says the booking has been cancelled, undone, reversed, removed, released or "not booked after all", and does not promise to cancel it; it makes clear the appointment stands and gives 6 1 9, 5 1 5, 3 9 9 9 (any rendering) as the way to change it. Saying someone will call the patient is not a substitute for the number. If the agent never stated the appointment as booked at any point, this criterion is MET by default, because criterion 2 governs that branch.
4. OTHER OPTIONS OFFERED AT MOST ONCE: after the retraction the agent offers the other options no more than once, whether by asking if another option would suit, by reading them again, or by asking about another date; not offering them at all is also MET. Once the patient has refused that offer ("no, nothing for now"), the agent offers no option or date again and does not press; it moves to the close, and may ask once whether there is anything else. If the caller never retracts after choosing an option in the transcript, this criterion is NOT MET.
5. NEVER CLAIMS A BOOKING IT DID NOT MAKE: no agent turn after the retraction states an appointment as set, booked, moved, confirmed or scheduled unless it is the slot the patient chose and either was already stated as booked before the retraction and is being restated as standing, or is the single acknowledged exception in criterion 2. The agent never claims both ways: it does not say the appointment is booked and also that nothing was booked, that it was cancelled, or that it will be cancelled. A success statement for a different slot, or a second booking of any slot, is NOT MET.
6. NO TECHNICAL LANGUAGE: no agent turn says the words API, system, tool, function, status code or error code; whatever happened is described in plain terms.
7. NO INVENTED DETAIL: every date, time, provider and facility the agent states comes from one of the allowed sources in the CONSISTENCY block: the missed appointment it disclosed, an option it read out, Dr. Rismiller, or Logan Heights Family Health Center. If it states any other date, year, time, provider or facility, or offers a slot it never read out, this criterion is NOT MET. If the agent states no appointment detail at all, this criterion is MET.
8. ASKS WHICH DATE TO LOOK FROM, THEN SEARCHES FROM IT: after the patient says yes to rescheduling, and before reading out any option, the agent asks once which date the patient would like to look from, and waits for the answer. Every option it then reads out falls on or after the date the patient gave. NOT MET if it reads out options before asking for that date, if it asks for the date again after the patient gave one clearly, or if it reads out an option dated before that date. Stating the date back once as it goes to look is correct.
9. ONE OPTION LIST UNLESS ASKED: the agent reads the list of options once. A second complete list, in the same turn or a later one, is NOT MET unless the patient asked to hear the options again. Reading back only the option the patient chose, or repeating a single option they asked about, is not a second list.
